script: Spread and total were not saved for NYG@WAS, so this Week 5 script is inferred only from form, not from a posted number. New York's last three games were Cam Skattebo's offense — 50 carries, 154 yards — with the NYG quarterback at -0.55 EPA per dropback versus the blitz, and Washington blitzes 47%, so the Giants should funnel touches to Skattebo instead of asking Malik Nabers (195 air yards on 17 targets) or Malachi Fields (205 air yards on 11 targets) to win downfield. Washington's form is a split backfield: Jacory Croskey-Merritt has the volume (40 carries, 94 yards, 2.35 YPC) while Rachaad White is the efficient piece (15 carries, 78 yards, 5.2 YPC) into a Giants run defense allowing 4.88 YPC.
who_goes_off: Cam Skattebo is the Giant who should go off in the short game: 9 targets, 67 receiving yards and only 32 air yards over three games, the dump-off profile when Washington pressures 47% of dropbacks. Rachaad White is the Washington skill player set up to produce, pairing 5.2 YPC on 15 carries with 7 targets and 46 receiving yards against a Giants defense that has allowed 11 runs of 10-plus yards.
weak_spot: Washington's real hole is the middle, not the outside corners: 11.36 yards per attempt on 25 middle throws versus 4.45 on 49 left-side attempts and 8.32 on 62 right-side attempts, so the matchup is linebackers, nickel and safeties. Isaiah Likely's 27 targets and 181 air yards are the Giants' volume answer to that middle leak, but a -0.55 EPA blitz split caps how often New York can exploit it. The Giants' weak spot is the run front — 4.88 YPC allowed and 11 gains of 10-plus — while their pass defense has allowed only 8 passes of 20-plus yards on 138 attempts.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for NYG@WAS, so there is no injury fallout to price; usage is only the last-three counts, led by Cam Skattebo's 50 carries and Isaiah Likely's 27 targets for New York and by Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 40 carries and Stefon Diggs' 22 targets for Washington.
qb_vs_blitz: Jameis Winston is the mismatch: the NYG quarterback is -0.55 EPA per dropback versus the blitz on 38 dropbacks and +0.28 with no blitz, and Washington brings pressure on 47% of dropbacks. Jayden Daniels is only -0.25 EPA versus the blitz on 31 dropbacks and +0.10 without it, and the Giants blitz just 34%, so Washington's quarterback spends more snaps in his playable split than Winston does.

picks.why: Cam Skattebo has 67 receiving yards on 9 targets over three games, 22.3 per game, against a 13.5 line, with just 32 air yards — a checkdown, not a shot play. Washington's 47% blitz rate meets a Winston split of -0.55 EPA on 38 dropbacks, which pushes New York to Skattebo rather than to Malik Nabers' 195 air yards on 17 targets.

Rachaad White has 78 rush yards plus 46 receiving yards over three games, 41.3 rush-plus-rec per game, against a 34 line, and he is already at 5.2 YPC on 15 carries. The Giants allow 4.88 YPC and 11 runs of 10-plus, and his 7 targets add a floor that Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 2.35 YPC on 40 carries does not.
